classification.habit: Prickly, creeping or ascending perennial herb/subshrub
classification.habitat: Open disturbed ground, grassland and moist tropical sites
classification.distribution: Widespread in tropical regions; naturalized in many parts of India

identification.description: Prickly sensitive plant with bipinnate leaves that fold on touch and small globose pinkish flower heads.
identification.whole_plant: Low, spreading or ascending prickly herb with sensitive foliage.
identification.root: Slender root system; traditional material may use root, but authentication is important.
identification.stem: Creeping to ascending, branched and armed with small prickles.
identification.leaf: Bipinnate, with numerous small leaflets; leaflets fold rapidly when touched.
identification.flower: Small globose heads, usually pink to lilac, borne on slender peduncles.
identification.fruit: Small flattened pods, often bristly, breaking into segments at maturity.
identification.seed: Small, hard seeds enclosed in segmented pods.
identification.bark: Not a true bark-bearing tree structure.

therapeutics.precautions: Traditional indications should not be treated as proof of clinical efficacy.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Mimosa pudica is notable for rapid leaf-folding movement and is widely studied botanically; traditional medicinal uses require evidence-specific interpretation.
modern_information.safety_notes: Avoid substituting similarly appearing Mimosa species; verify identity before medicinal use.

exam_points: Diagnostic feature: leaves fold on touch
viva_questions: Which family does it belong to?
mnemonics: Lajjalu = leaf becomes shy on touch
student.quick_revision: Lajjalu—Mimosa pudica; Fabaceae; sensitive bipinnate leaves; prickly herb.

teaching_points: Use the specimen to teach Fabaceae morphology.
discussion_points: Differentiate Lajjalu from other sensitive or prickly legumes.
Discuss botanical movement versus medicinal claims.
practical_points: Observe leaf response without excessive repeated handling.
Examine prickles, flower head and segmented pod.

doctor.quick_reference: Traditional Lajjalu profile emphasizes stambhana and wound-related contexts.
key_precautions: Confirm botanical identity before medicinal use.
